A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SynCoGen, with matching authors, core methods, and retained experiments. Their complete main texts and appendices provide readable equations, tables, and figures, allowing additions to be distinguished from relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecule-generation experiments, training and sampling ablations, conformer evaluations, and fragment-linking results in Tables 1–6 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds larger-vocabulary experiments, pharmacophore-conditioned generation, fine-tuned fragment linking, and additional chemical analyses.

M1.justification: v2 adds a pharmacophore-conditioning backbone with a separate feature head, concatenated pharmacophore coordinates, and zero centering weight for pharmacophore features (Section 4.1). It also introduces an inpainting fine-tuning variant. These extend the procedure beyond v1's unconditional generator and zero-shot inpainting, while retaining the original joint diffusion/flow mechanism.

E1.justification: v2 adds SynSpace-L, expanding represented chemistry from 93 building blocks and 19 reaction templates to 378 blocks and 26 templates. It also evaluates a distinct pharmacophore-conditioned task on ten targets, including seven from LIT-PCBA, while retaining v1's three fragment-linking targets.

E2.justification: The new conditional-generation comparison evaluates SynFormer, ShEPhERD, and CGFlow-ZS against SynCoGen (Figure 5). Figure 19 additionally compares random SynSpace and FDA-approved molecules as controls. The original Table 1 comparator set, including SynSpace-trained SemlaFlow, and the DiffLinker comparison are retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a ten-target protocol generating 100 molecules per method and target, with baseline-specific conditioning procedures. It adds five-epoch inpainting fine-tuning and controlled larger-vocabulary and edge-sampling evaluations. Section 5.1 also revises the stated diversity metric from Tanimoto similarity to dissimilarity; unchanged Table 1 values do not establish recomputation.

E4.justification: New analyses examine probabilistic versus argmax edge sampling, larger-vocabulary behavior, dataset physicochemical properties, fine-tuning, and hard-to-synthesize chemical features. Figure 19 tests how much docking performance reflects conditioning versus the curated chemical space. The original training and schedule ablations remain as v2 Tables 3–4 rather than being newly introduced.

E5.justification: The statement reporting averages over three random-seed runs for unconditional baselines is retained. v2 adds no confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run uncertainty estimates. Its new docking boxplots summarize variation across generated molecules.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the original fragment-linking rows retain their numerical results. Substantial new results include SynCoGen's 86.3% validity and 61%/78% retrosynthesis solve rates in Figure 5, larger-vocabulary outcomes, and fine-tuned inpainting rows in Table 8. These are added experimental results, not same-setting improvements to the retained unconditional benchmark.

T1.justification: Sections 3.3 and 4.1 add mathematical definitions of pharmacophore feature and coordinate tensors and their mappings into augmented model inputs. The original diffusion objectives, posterior equations, losses, and equivariance qualification remain substantially unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or theoretical guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion broaden the contribution from one dataset and zero-shot linker design to a dataset family and amortized pharmacophore-conditioned design. v2 claims superior conditional performance across diverse targets without external scoring functions or target-specific retraining, substantially extending v1's narrower demonstrated application claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of vocabulary scaling and its geometry-quality tradeoff. Figure 19 attributes part of docking performance to building-block curation and explicitly cautions that docking only proxies binding affinity. The conclusion calls for experimental synthesis and binding validation. Existing chemistry simplifications and the non-equivariance caveat are retained, although the latter moves to the appendix.

D1.justification: v2 documents pharmacophore preprocessing and conditioning, conditional-baseline inference settings, atom-count sampling, and fine-tuning details. Its new reproducibility statement describes pretrained checkpoints, configuration and evaluation scripts, and custom-dataset generation. The original code/data URLs and hardware information are retained; their relocation is not a new resource release.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to ShEPhERD, TacoGFN, and LIT-PCBA, and explicitly contrasts its amortized design with CGFlow's reward optimization and target-specific training. Most of the related-work discussion and cited literature remain unchanged; expanded author names and citation formatting are bibliographic presentation changes.

P1.justification: v2 substantially revises the abstract, conclusion, and coordinate-noising explanation, moves main-text pseudocode into Appendix B, and introduces a stepwise training and masking walkthrough. It reorganizes the experimental appendices and adds ethics and reproducibility statements. These are substantial explanatory and structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds pharmacophore comparison plots, expanded-vocabulary illustrations, dataset-property plots, training/masking diagrams, and additional analysis tables. Figure 3 is condensed, with its omitted panels incorporated into appendix Figure 14. The original training-ablation table moves to the appendix, the inpainting table gains fine-tuning rows, and the document adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence for conditional molecular design and scaling beyond v1's small vocabulary through a new conditioning method, ten-target comparisons, larger-vocabulary tests, and controls separating conditioning benefits from library curation. The explanatory diagrams and reproducibility details also improve assessability. These gains are qualified by lower PoseBusters validity in the larger-vocabulary experiment and the continued absence of experimental synthesis or binding validation; v2 explicitly acknowledges the limits of docking evidence.
